# KineMech

> KineMech is a free, open-source planar mechanism simulator that runs in the browser at https://kinemech.app/. It handles general planar mechanisms of any topology, not only the textbook four-bar and slider-crank: multi-loop linkages and six-bars, gear trains, pin-in-slot joints, and cam-follower pairs. For any of them it computes kinematics, joint forces (kinetostatics), and forward dynamics, the motion a mechanism makes under applied torques and loads. It also synthesizes linkages and designs cams and gears. Version 5.0.0, MIT license, by Tareq Zobaer.

KineMech has four tools that hand designs to each other: the Analyzer (kinematics, forces, dynamics simulation and vibration), the Synthesizer (linkage synthesis), the Profiler (cam design and follower dynamics) and Gears (gear design).

## What it does

- Mechanisms: any planar mechanism built from pin, slider, slot, gear and cam joints, with binary, ternary and higher-order links and any number of loops. Examples include four-bars, slider-cranks, Whitworth and shaper quick-return mechanisms, a five-cylinder radial engine, a Stephenson six-bar, the Jansen walking linkage, geared linkages, plate cams, conjugate cams, and one cam driving followers of different types.
- Kinematics: position, velocity and acceleration of every joint and link, including Coriolis terms, by Newton-Raphson on the general constraint equations. Velocity and acceleration polygons, degrees-of-freedom checks, dead-point and change-point detection, Grashof classification and transmission angle. The instant center of every pair with its Kennedy construction, velocity of slip, mechanical advantage, fixed and moving centrodes, and jerk.
- Forces (kinetostatics): joint reactions and the input torque or force a prescribed motion needs, with mass and inertia, gravity, point loads, torques, linear and torsional springs and dampers, cam contact force and follower jump, gear mesh force, shaking force and moment, free-body diagrams, the input torque checked by virtual work, and counterweight balancing on any links, with the classical four-bar and slider-crank constructions, force against moment, and two correction planes.
- Dynamics (forward dynamics simulation): apply a torque or force to the input (constant, a DC motor line, a speed controller, a harmonic, or a table over time or input angle) and simulate the motion it gives, with fixed-step or adaptive integration. Loads can follow tables over time or crank angle. Every run reports kinetic and potential energy with an energy balance, stops at a follower jump, a change point or an input limit, or carries on through input limits. A flywheel can be sized from the constant-speed cycle and its speed fluctuation checked in a simulation.
- Vibration: the mechanism linearized about its rest position as a single-degree-of-freedom system, with equivalent inertia, stiffness and damping at the input, natural frequency, damping ratio, damped period, logarithmic decrement, the steady response to a harmonic effort and the magnification factor, checked against a simulated release.
- Synthesis: four-bar motion generation (two to four positions), path generation (precision points, or fitting a whole target curve), function generation (Freudenstein, three to five points), quick-return mechanisms, and single- and double-dwell six-bars, with Grashof, transmission-angle and defect checks.
- Cam design: plate, cylindrical and linear cams from rise-dwell-fall programs in eight motion laws, knife-edge, roller, flat-face and spherical followers, pressure angle and undercut checks, and the graphical construction drawn out.
- Follower dynamics: the cam follower as a mass on an elastic follower train with a preloaded return spring and damping, in steady running or from rest, with every result beside the rigid follower's: actual against commanded motion, dynamic amplification, contact force and the preload needed to keep contact, residual vibration in each dwell, the residual vibration spectrum of each motion law, and the rigid and elastic jump speeds.
- Gear design: external, internal and rack involute meshes with standard and custom tooth systems, profile shift, generated roots and undercut, contact ratio and interference checks, and fixed-axis and planetary gear trains solved from known speeds.
- Units: masses in kg, inertias in kg·m², forces in N, torques in N·m, with a physical length unit (m, cm, mm, in, ft) so drawings at any scale give real forces.
- Output: plots against crank angle or time, CSV, animated GIF, and `.kinemech`, `.kinepath`, `.kinemotion` and `.kinegears` files.
